title: Per-tenant Latency SLO via Token-bucket QoS and Kernel-aware Micro-scheduler
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Tenants on Dedicated GPU pools sometimes experience intermittent latency spikes due to noisy neighbors and bursty KV-cache / batch patterns. Current large-grain lane allocation can protect throughput but fails to guarantee p95/p99 latency for customers with strict SLAs.

Goal: Implement a per-tenant soft QoS mechanism that enforces latency SLOs without hard-slicing GPUs. Approach combines a token-bucket at the request-routing layer, short-lived kernel-aware micro-scheduling decisions on worker processes, and an autoscaling integration that converts sustained token deficits into proactive scale-up or lane rebalance actions. This ticket scopes the design, prototype, and rollout plan for the control plane + runtime changes required to enforce p95 latency targets for Dedicated tenants under noisy neighbor load while preserving unit efficiency for bursty customers.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can configure per-tenant p95 and p99 latency SLOs as part of a Dedicated plan
Runner enforces a token-bucket throttle tied to SLO that is visible in tracing and metrics
Micro-scheduler reduces multi-tenant interference: median and p95 latency regressions <10% vs baseline under synthetic noisy loads
Autoscaler triggers proactive capacity increase when token deficit sustained for configurable window
Rollout can be toggled per-tenant and has an automated rollback path on error conditions
implementation_notes:
High-level components: (1) QoS controller in control plane to accept SLO config and compute token rates per-tenant; (2) edge/routing middleware to attach token budget info to requests and emit token metrics; (3) runtime micro-scheduler in the worker loop that uses a lightweight kernel-aware backoff (cgroup cpu.weight adjustments + nanosleep windows) to defer non-critical batches when tenant budget low; (4) autoscaler hook that converts sustained token shortage to scale requests or lane reassignments. We will keep default behavior permissive (soft throttle) for first rollout, with an opt-in hard-throttling mode later. For observability, instrument per-tenant token usage, deficit duration, deferral reasons, and correlated p95/p99 metrics.

Trade-offs considered: Hard slicing yields strict isolation but wastes capacity and increases costs. Pure autoscaling reacts too slowly to sudden noisy spikes. Token-bucket + micro-scheduler offers bounded latency protection while preserving statistical multiplexing. Risk: incorrectly tuned backoff can increase tail latency for low-priority tenants; mitigated by conservative initial rate limits and AB tests.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for token accounting and rate enforcement. 2) Integration harness: synthetic multi-tenant workload generator that can produce KV-cache heavy and large-batch patterns. 3) Load tests in staging with controlled noisy neighbors: measure median/p95/p99 latency and throughput. 4) Chaos test: introduce transient GPU slowdowns and ensure rollback doesn't cascade. 5) Gradual canary: 5% of Dedicated fleet -> 25% -> 100% based on success metrics. Monitoring: dashboards for token deficit, inflight batches deferred, tenant-level SLO pass rate.
comments: 2026-03-02 -- Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes posted. Consensus to avoid hard GPU slice for now; focus on soft QoS + autoscaler integration. Action: Diego to prototype token-bucket in edge layer.

2026-03-04 -- Diego Alvarez: PoC implemented in the routing middleware. Token accounting lives in Redis for now to simplify cross-worker visibility. Initial tests show 15% reduction in p95 for target tenant under synthetic noise. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/312

2026-03-06 -- Design review (Anika Patel): Suggested adding per-tenant emergency budget to allow short bursts that temporarily exceed SLO without immediate autoscale. We'll add a burn-rate limiter and expose burn budget in the API.

2026-03-08 -- QA (Ravi Singh): Staging run: workload with three tenants (SLO, best-effort, noisy) showed p99 improvements for SLO tenant but small throughput loss for best-effort. Left action: quantify cost impact and add a 'best-effort' label to minimize impact on free-tier tenants.
2026-03-10 -- Security (Lila Morgan): Security review request submitted; no secrets change but Redis token store must be on VPC-only subnet. Marked ticket for security_review_required.
next_steps: 1) Finalize micro-scheduler heuristic and land runtime PR. 2) Replace Redis PoC with embedded distributed counter via our control plane cache. 3) Run staged canary and collect SLO metrics. 4) Post-mortem template and rollback runbook to be added to the release doc.
notes: Prototype uses conservative defaults: token_bucket_capacity=2x median-inflight, deficit_window=10s, backoff_base=5ms. These will be tunable per-tenant. We will revisit kernel tuning flags (sched_latency_ns) only if micro-scheduler shows measurable gains; aim to keep changes to user-space where possible.
